knowledgePattern: Bound a distance sum before optimising the outer quadratic

hints.title: Interpret the inner expression
hints.body: Read each modulus as a distance on a number line. Find the smallest possible sum and where it is attained.
hints.recap: A modulus represents distance on the number line; a shifted input measures distance from the corresponding point.
hints.pitfall: An inner lower bound needs an input that actually attains it.
hints.pause: Determine the full allowed range of f.

recall.reminder: A modulus represents distance on the number line; a shifted input measures distance from the corresponding point.

hints.title: Restrict the quadratic
hints.body: Complete the square in the outer function, but only compare inputs that belong to the inner range.
hints.recap: An outer vertex gives an attainable extreme only if its input belongs to the inner range.
hints.pitfall: The vertex of g may not be reached by f.
hints.pause: Find the least permitted outer value and verify attainment.

recall.reminder: An outer vertex gives an attainable extreme only if its input belongs to the inner range.

solution:
1. The sum |x−2|+|x+2| is the distance from −2 to x and then to 2. It is at least 4, with equality throughout [−2,2]. Outside this interval it equals 2|x|, so its full range is [4,∞).

2. Write t=f(x). Then g(t)=(t−1)2+3. On t≥4, this increases as t increases, so its minimum occurs at t=4.

3. The minimum is g(4)=16−8+4=12, attained for every x∈[−2,2]. Answer C.
